narrative:
The model predicts you have a 19% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your lack of desire to pursue higher education, your reason for choosing this school, and the fact that you have had no previous class failures. Your stated intention not to continue studying beyond high school was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward failure. Because nearly every student who passes wants to go on to higher education, your answer stood out as a clear warning sign that you may not be fully committed to finishing strongly.

Your choice of this school because of its reputation pushed the prediction in the opposite direction and helped the model somewhat. Most students who pass chose the school for its academic program rather than its reputation, so this factor worked in your favor, though not enough to outweigh the other influences.

Surprisingly, having zero past failures also nudged the prediction slightly toward failing. While this is the same clean record as the average student who passes, the model appears to have interpreted it in context with your other answers as meaning you may not have faced the kind of challenges that build resilience.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on why you no longer want to continue your studies and whether that view can change. Setting clearer goals, reducing time spent going out with friends, and cutting down on the 12 absences you accumulated this year would also help you finish the year successfully.
